# The internet and social movements

## Gezi Park Protests


![Gezi Park](images/İstanbul_-_Taksim_Gezi_Parkı_-_Mart_2013_-_r4.jpg){width="90%"}



::: notes
-   Beginning May 27, 2013 and ending in mid August

-   Initially an encampment style protest against a plan to develop the Gezi park area, but turned into a generalized protest against Erdogan

:::

## Gezi Park Protests

```{r, fig.width=10}
vdem<-vdemdata::vdem|>
  filter(country_name =='Türkiye')|>
  filter(year>=1945)|>
  mutate(date = as.Date(paste0(year, "-01-01")))



yvalue<-vdem$v2x_libdem[which(vdem$year==2003)]
yvalue2<-vdem$v2x_libdem[which(vdem$year==2013)]

vdem|>
ggplot(
       aes(x=date, y=v2x_libdem)) + geom_line(lty=1, lwd=1) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(y='Liberal-Democracy score',
       x="Year",
       title = "Turkey liberal democracy since 1945",
       caption ='Source: VDEM 2020'
       ) +
 # geom_vline(xintercept=as.Date('2003-03-14'), 
#             lty =2
#             ) +
  geom_segment(x=as.Date('2003-03-14'), xend=as.Date('2003-03-14'), y=0, yend=yvalue, lty=2) +
  annotate(geom='label', x=as.Date('2003-03-14')+2500, y=0.525, 
           label='Erdoğan becomes PM') +
  geom_segment(x=as.Date('2013-05-27'), xend=as.Date('2013-05-27'), y=0, yend=yvalue2, lty=2) +
  annotate(geom='label', x=as.Date('2013-05-27')+ 2200, y=yvalue2, 
           label='Gezi Park protests')



```




## Gezi Park and social media


- Not the first protest to use twitter, but notable for the sheer volume of social media activity related to the protests and their perceived importance for activists and opponents:



> "Now we have a menace that is called Twitter… To me, social media is the worst menace to society" - Recep Tayyip Erdoğan

## The internet and contentious politics


::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: incremental
- There's some consensus that the internet "matters" for contentious actors

- There's not a consensus on whether it is a net positive or a net negative and how fundamentally it changes the calculus for contentious behavior.

:::

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/gezi_bird.jpg)
:::
:::::




## The internet as a tool


::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

-   Information sharing (even under repression)

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

![](images/inspire_magazine.jpg) Inspire Magazine: online publication released by Al-Qaeda

:::::

## The internet as a tool


::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

-   Information sharing (even under repression)

-   Mobilization, framing and identity building (without the need for mainstream press coverage or direct social interaction) 

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

![](images/tufekci_facebook_protest.png)
[@tufekci2012social]

:::
:::::


## The internet as a tool

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A study of Gezi park social media activity found connections to the "periphery" were critical for spreading the messages and experiences of participants.  [@barbera2015critical]


:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/barbera_core.png)
:::
:::::


## The internet as a venue


::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

- The internet itself is increasingly a *site* of contention:
  - Online boycotts
  - Coordinated harassment or pressure campaigns
  - Politically motivated hacks

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![Wikipedia's SOPA/PIPA blackout message](images/wikipedia_blackout_screen.jpg)

:::
:::::



## Reasons for skepticism

### High risk activism

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   Classic Studies of "high-risk" activism found that strong social ties were key: committed activists are part of a community.

-   ICT facilitated movements are wide-but-shallow. 



:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/McAdam_recruitment.png)
:::
:::::


### Slacktivism

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

::: incremental
- **Catharsis** is the process of getting relief from an emotion by expressing it. 

- **Slacktivism** refers to low-cost, low risk activities that express support or raise awareness of an issue. 

- Taken together: opportunities for slacktivism might sap energy that would otherwise lead people to more impactful forms of participation

:::

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

```{=html}
</div>
```

:::

## Online repression

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

- Social media is centralized and less anonymous than might be assumed, so they can make systematic low-level repression easier.

- The same resource advantages that favor corporate and state actors offline are mirrored in online spaces.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/wikipedia_scientology.png)

:::
:::::



## Online repression

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

- States have gotten much better at repressing online contention over time.


- [@king2013censorship] found evidence of industrial-scale censorship of Chinese social media posts. Primarily targeted at efforts to mobilize people for offline activity.

:::
::: {.column width="50%"}

![](images/china_censorship.png)


:::
:::::
